physical_mismatches.reason: The original model is a 2.5D multi-chiplet system on an interposer with NoP/D2D links, die-to-die spacing (ICS 2.3 mm) and a TIM/heat spreader/heat sink stack. A simple 2D single-die runner cannot reproduce the inter-chiplet lateral coupling, interposer heat spreading or NoP power distribution.

The power input is an average derived from analytical energy/latency models over a sequential multi-DNN workload. It is not a transient power trace, and the paper models no transient thermal behavior, only steady state.

The paper does not publish per-block floorplan coordinates, block dimensions or per-block power for the selected design. Only aggregate parameters are given: core/chiplet counts, ICS, buffer size, systolic array size, and total energy and delay. A block-level replication is therefore impossible.

The optimizer is TED+SCBO Bayesian optimization co-optimizing architecture and task mapping, with no runtime controller. A Studio runner has no equivalent optimizer, so only the thermal solve could be exercised.
The cooling model (convection resistance 0.4 K/W, 45 C ambient, TESA material properties) and the HotSpot 6.0 package stack may differ from the Studio's bundled material and package assumptions.
Reliability is not modeled beyond the 75 C peak limit. Yield is modeled analytically from die area and is unrelated to thermal reliability.

studio_assumptions: No paper-derived floorplan exists, so any runner placement would be a separately generated illustrative 2D layout with generated coordinates kept distinct from paper facts.
Studio uses its own bundled package and material stack, which is not guaranteed to match the paper's HotSpot 6.0 interposer/TIM/spreader/heat-sink configuration (TESA properties).
Studio runs a 2D thermal solve, not the paper's 2.5D interposer model.
Any one-row power trace would be illustrative only, and Studio temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 74.8 C.
